question.problem:
$$
f(x,z)=⟨x,\,\text{_____},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(x,z)$ above parametrizes the hyperbolic paraboloid defined in Cartesian coordinates as $3y={z}^{2}-9{x}^{2}.$ What is the second component of $f?$
question.worked_solution:
Solving our equation for $y,$ we obtain

$$
3y={z}^{2}-9{x}^{2}\,⟹\,y=\frac{{z}^{2}}{3}-3{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨x,\,\frac{{z}^{2}}{3}-3{x}^{2},\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $x\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $\frac{{z}^{2}}{3}-3{x}^{2}.$
